general_notes: Across all four states the candidates fall into five consistent groups: (1) the target with a flat border frame (near-perfect), (2) a heavily blurred copy (character intact in shape and colour but texture destroyed), (3) a round soft vignette on dark that keeps some painted background, (4) a hard near-black background with tight vignette that loses outer embers/smoke and the painted ambience, and (5) a 3D/vector re-creation of the character that differs substantially. Several candidates within a state appear pixel-identical to each other (e.g. idle A/C/E, idle B/D, joyful A/C/E, joyful F/H, fierce A/E, fierce D/G/H, depleted A/C, depleted B/F roughly); I scored them identically except where I could see a difference (depleted D is darker than B/F). The vignetted versions are also somewhat softer/lower-resolution than the target, which I folded into P1. The depleted target itself contains a grey rectangular patch at lower right; candidates that remove it were not penalised on character dims. Judgements are visual only at the displayed resolution; fine differences within the vignette group could be missed.
